title: Three truths
hookLine: Tiantai: emptiness, the provisional and the middle, all at once

lines: OPEN IT. WHERE DID IT GO?
cards: Make a fist. Go on, either hand. There it is: a fist.
Now open your fingers. Where did the fist go? It didn't fly off anywhere.

There was never a fist apart from the hand curled up a certain way. And yet, a moment ago, it was a real fist; you could have knocked on a door with it. So which is true: there's no fist, or there's a fist?
Tiantai's answer is yes. And then it adds a third thing. Tiantai calls them the three truths.

teach.b: It starts with a verse by the Indian teacher Nagarjuna, read in Chinese, which says in substance: whatever arises from conditions, that is emptiness; it is a name given in dependence; and that is the middle way.
Zhiyi read that one verse and heard three truths in it. Emptiness: the fist has no fist-ness of its own. It's made of a hand, a moment, a squeeze; take those away and nothing is left over.
The provisional: and still, the fist works. It has a name, it can knock, it's a real fist in the world of fists, even though it depends on everything else. The middle: the two aren't taking turns.
The fist isn't empty on Monday and real on Tuesday.
It is empty and real in the same instant, and the middle is simply that togetherness. Then Zhiyi's turn.
Some teachers treated these as levels: first you see things as real, then you climb to see them as empty, then, at the top, the middle.
Tiantai calls that one way of teaching.
Its own reading is that the three are perfectly joined, each truth containing the other two.
Look all the way into emptiness and the provisional world is right there; look closely at the plain world and the middle is right there. The school says this isn't a puzzle to win.
It's a way of seeing a doorway, a quarrel, a face, without falling into either ditch, it's all nothing or it's all solid, and walking the middle of the road.

how: Tiantai and Tendai Buddhists study the three truths, emptiness, the provisional and the middle, and use them as a way of contemplating any object or moment in meditation.

o: three vows a Tiantai monk takes on the mountain
everything is empty, provisionally real, and the middle at once
three sutras that hold the whole of the Buddha's word

games.q: the three truths: tap the pairs.
p: it has a name and does its job
the verse Zhiyi read three ways

s: for Tiantai, the three truths are steps you climb one by one
Tiantai calls that one way of teaching; its own reading is that the three are perfectly joined.
the three truths come from Zhiyi's reading of a verse by Nagarjuna
a verse on emptiness, dependent naming and the middle way.
emptiness means the fist was never real at all
it was a real fist. it just had no fist-ness of its own.

games.q: you open your hand and the fist is gone. someone asks you: was the fist real? how would Tiantai answer?
o: no, it was only ever a hand.
yes, and nothing more needs saying.
empty and real at once, and that togetherness is the middle.
games.why: Tiantai holds all three together. each truth contains the other two.

practice: Pick something in front of you, a pen, a shoe, your own hand, and for a few breaths look at it as empty: made of parts and causes, nothing in it that stands alone.
Then for a few breaths look at it as provisional: it has a name, it does its job, it's really here. Then let both be true together, without choosing or straining for a special feeling, and breathe.

wordCard.voice: Three truths. Tiantai's teaching that every thing is empty, provisionally real, and the middle, all in one moment, each holding the others. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese sandi: the three truths of Tiantai.
